stories.title: Air India Express app update offers 10% discount
stories.summary: Air India Express has launched an updated mobile app featuring integrated booking, check-in, and boarding services. To encourage adoption, the airline is offering first-time users a 10% discount on base fares. The carrier aims to simplify the passenger journey by consolidating travel services onto a single platform.

stories.title: Air India and Air India Express to merge support functions
stories.summary: Air India and its subsidiary Air India Express plan to integrate support functions to address rising operational costs. CEO Tewolde Gebremariam announced the strategy following combined losses of USD 2.33 billion. Both airlines will maintain separate operating certificates while coordinating more closely on regulatory and operational tasks.

stories.title: Raymond to operate Worli jetty helipad
stories.summary: The BMC has approved a 15-year agreement for Raymond Ltd to develop and operate a DGCA-licensed helipad at Mumbai's Worli jetty. The facility is intended to support emergency evacuations, disaster response, and coastal surveillance. The site currently extends 120 metres into the Arabian Sea.

stories.title: IndiGo invests in air taxi venture
stories.summary: IndiGo has invested 10 crore rupees in Sarla Aviation to support the development of an electric vertical take-off and landing aircraft network. The partnership focuses on short-distance routes between 30 km and 300 km. The airline aims to leverage its operational experience to expand into air taxi services.

stories.title: BMC approves Worli jetty helipad project
stories.summary: The BMC Standing Committee has approved Raymond Ltd as the operator for a 15-year project to convert Worli jetty into a DGCA-licensed helipad. The facility will be equipped for emergency evacuations, security operations, and VVIP movements. The jetty extends 120 metres into the Arabian Sea.

stories.title: Man finds workaround for airport cab pricing
stories.summary: A passenger at Mumbai Airport claimed to have reduced a 1,500 rupee cab fare to 79 rupees by walking outside the terminal to book his ride. The traveler shared the experience online after encountering high demand pricing and a 17-minute wait for a 4-km trip.

stories.title: Air India targets 60 billion rupee cost reduction
stories.summary: CEO Tewolde Gebremariam has announced a 60 billion rupee cost-cutting plan for the current fiscal year, involving department mergers and a flight network reshuffle. The airline is also introducing holiday packages to generate new revenue. The company is currently working to improve its financial performance.

stories.title: Air India to launch in-house tour operations
stories.summary: Air India plans to establish an in-house tour operations unit to offer holiday packages in collaboration with the Ministry of Tourism. CEO Tewolde Gebremariam stated the business could become a significant revenue stream. The group has identified 3,500 crore rupees in potential savings toward a 6,000 crore target.

stories.title: Air India outlines fiscal turnaround strategy
stories.summary: Air India has set a cost-reduction target of 6,000 crore rupees for the current financial year. CEO Tewolde Gebremariam reported that 1,500 crore rupees in savings have been achieved so far. The airline previously recorded losses exceeding 22,000 crore rupees in the prior financial year.

stories.title: Air Canada named best in North America
stories.summary: Air Canada has been named the best airline in North America at the 2026 Skytrax World Airline Awards for the second consecutive year. The Montreal-based carrier outperformed Delta, Porter, and United Airlines to secure the title. The awards were announced in London this fall.

stories.title: Breeze Airways routes show low load factors
stories.summary: Data from the Bureau of Transportation Statistics indicates that several Breeze Airways routes are operating below the 80% load factor typically required for profitability. While the carrier's average load factor is 77.9%, some routes are currently at 22% capacity as the airline expands its point-to-point network.

stories.title: Allegiant Air adds 16 Florida routes
stories.summary: Allegiant Air is launching 16 new routes to Florida, a state that accounts for 65% of the carrier's total flights. Despite operating 115 daily departures, the airline remains the sixth-largest domestic operator in the state. Flight activity varies significantly between weekdays and Sundays.

stories.title: Delta and United continue aging 757-300 fleets
stories.summary: Delta Air Lines and United Airlines continue to operate Boeing 757-300 aircraft, a model neither airline originally intended to purchase. The carriers acquired the jets through corporate dealings with other operators. Both airlines maintain the fleet for its specific capacity and range capabilities.

stories.title: United Airlines to launch Sapporo route
stories.summary: United Airlines will begin nonstop service between San Francisco and Sapporo on December 11. The route is intended to capture winter travel demand for the region's ski resorts. It will serve as the airline's newest destination in Asia and its shortest international route to the continent.

stories.title: Norse Atlantic suspends operations
stories.summary: Norse Atlantic has suspended all flights following a collapse in its stock price and warnings of a financial crisis. The board of directors is currently exploring options to secure short-term financing. The suspension has left passengers stranded during the holiday period.

stories.title: Norse Atlantic Airways suspends all flights as carrier faces bankruptcy - Sky News
Schiphol extends airline charge discounts
stories.summary: Amsterdam Airport Schiphol will extend a 10% discount on airport charges for airlines through March 2028. The relief is intended to help carriers manage rising jet fuel costs. Night flights remain excluded from the discount, and the airport continues to charge higher fees for noisier aircraft.

stories.title: Norse Atlantic warns of potential bankruptcy
stories.summary: Norwegian carrier Norse Atlantic has suspended all flights and is in talks to sell its business due to a liquidity shortage. The decision followed an 85% drop in the company's share price. The board is currently seeking short-term financing to avoid filing for bankruptcy.

stories.title: At Mérignac, Dassault Aviation honors its 170 suppliers - Aerocontact.com
GE wins deal from Malaysia Aviation Group to supply GEnx engines
Trump hints at 250-aircraft order from China
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump suggested Chinese carriers could order 250 more aircraft, following a 200-aircraft Boeing order from May 2026. The president also claimed credit for a recent Philippine Airlines order, asserting he prevented the carrier from going to Europe. The airline has not commented on his involvement.

stories.title: Airbus submits engine pylon factory project to public consultation
stories.summary: Airbus has entered a public consultation process for a new engine pylon factory in Cornebarrieu, France. The site is intended to replace the existing Saint-Eloi factory in central Toulouse to expand production capacity. The company says the location will benefit from synergies. The process began on November 24.

stories.title: New PIA CEO outlines aircraft order plan
stories.summary: Pakistan International Airlines CEO Adrian Hamilton-Manns plans to announce an order for up to 50 aircraft during the first quarter of 2027. Hamilton-Manns, who assumed the role on November 2, stated that the now-privatized airline is focusing on its fleet expansion strategy.

stories.title: Chinese airline places order for 50 Boeing jets
stories.summary: Xiamen Airlines will purchase 50 Boeing 737-8 aircraft for approximately US$7.4 billion. The deal includes a discount on the catalogue price, though the amount remains unspecified. Deliveries are scheduled between 2031 and 2034. The order follows President Trump's suggestion that China could purchase an additional 250 Boeing jets.

stories.title: Positive Aviation commits €60M to build firefighting ATR72s
stories.summary: French startup Positive Aviation is investing €60 million to build two manufacturing facilities for its amphibious firefighting ATR72 retrofit. The project is part of the France 2030 initiative, which selects industrial projects for state funding based on their strategic importance. The main facility will be located in Toulouse.

stories.title: Adani and Embraer negotiate joint venture structure
stories.summary: Adani Defence and Aerospace and Embraer are negotiating a joint venture to manufacture civilian aircraft in India. A disagreement over shareholding has emerged, with Adani seeking a 51 percent stake and Embraer maintaining that it requires 51 percent to ensure compliance with its quality assurance and technology transfer requirements.

stories.title: Babcock to expand Horn Island aviation base
stories.summary: Babcock Australasia is investing $10 million to expand its aviation base at Horn Island, Queensland. The project includes a new hangar capable of accommodating three medium-sized helicopters, intended to support Australian Border Force operations. The company has operated in the region for over 30 years.

stories.title: FAA runway rule change affects holiday departures
stories.summary: The FAA has restricted the "Line Up and Wait" procedure, requiring a dedicated supervisor to be on duty for its use. The rule took effect on November 24, coinciding with the start of the Thanksgiving travel period. The procedure allows airports to launch departures back-to-back.

stories.title: FAA reports flight delays
FAA warns of Thanksgiving arrival delays at New York airports
stories.summary: The FAA warned that arriving flights in the New York area could face delays or airborne holding of up to 30 minutes on Thanksgiving Day due to wind, rain, and low clouds. By noon on November 26, the agency had removed potential ground stops from its advisory plan.

stories.title: EASA extends conflict zone advisories
stories.summary: The European Union Aviation Safety Agency has extended conflict-zone advisories for the Persian Gulf, Gulf of Oman, Saudi Arabia, Iran, and Iraq until January 31, 2027. Airspace access remains subject to case-by-case assessments, permissions, and timing rather than blanket closures. Routing and fuel risks remain in the advisories.

stories.title: Air traffic controller warning preceded fatal crash
stories.summary: A pilot and five family members died when their aircraft crashed off the coast of Mississippi. Air traffic control had issued a warning regarding adverse weather in the area prior to the incident. The pilot did not report any problems during takeoff or the flight.

stories.title: Passenger recounts turbulent flight in Argentina
stories.summary: A passenger described a turbulent flight in Argentina, noting that high winds caused significant distress among travelers. The flight aborted its first landing attempt. The account appears in a publication exploring the economic policies of President Javier Milei, including the impact of airline deregulation on state monopolies.

stories.title: FAA ground stop timeline
stories.summary: A telecommunications issue caused a nationwide ground stop that lasted more than four hours. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy reported instability in radar and communications for Air Traffic Control centers. The incident occurred on a Friday, disrupting travel plans for millions of passengers.

stories.title: Air traffic controller shortage persists
stories.summary: Nav Canada reports a continued shortfall of air traffic controllers heading into the holiday season. The company notes that while the labor gap persists, delays related to staffing shortages have decreased significantly. The organization has not provided specific figures regarding the current number of vacancies.

stories.title: FAA restricts runway procedure
stories.summary: The FAA has tightened rules for the "Line Up and Wait" procedure, mandating that a supervisor who is not working other roles must be present in the tower. The change, implemented before Thanksgiving, makes tower staffing a direct limit on airport throughput.

stories.title: Pilots note design differences between Boeing 737 MAX and Airbus A320neo
stories.summary: Transitioning between the Boeing 737 MAX and Airbus A320neo involves moving between two different aviation design philosophies. The A320 family was built as a digital fly-by-wire system, while the 737 traces its origins to 1965. The two aircraft represent fundamentally different eras of aviation design history.

stories.title: NBAA examines barriers for veterans entering business aviation
stories.summary: The National Business Aviation Association has published interviews with three professionals regarding obstacles former US military personnel face when seeking civilian careers. The organization notes that the industry hiring pipeline relies more on informal networks and mentors than on formal recruiting channels, leaving departments with a talent pool.

stories.title: Air Arabia Academy sends cadets to Oman for flight training
stories.summary: Air Arabia Academy has sent a group of cadets to Oman to complete the Core Flying Phase of its Multi-Crew Pilot Licence training program. The activity continues the academy's cooperation arrangement with Oman Aviation Academy, which provides international flight training for the Sharjah-based carrier's pilot training division.

stories.title: ANA Holdings establishes in-house pilot training company
stories.summary: ANA Holdings has established ANA Next Aviation to train pilots ahead of mass retirements expected around 2030. The company will provide basic training at Kagoshima Airport, moving operations previously outsourced to overseas providers in-house. It is the first pilot training provider created by an airline for its own use.

stories.title: Thérèse Peltier and the first flight by a woman
stories.summary: On 8 July 1908, French sculptor Thérèse Peltier sat beside pilot Léon Delagrange in a Voisin biplane in Turin. The aircraft flew for approximately 200 to 250 metres before returning to the hangar. By most accounts, this event marked the first time a woman flew in an aeroplane.

stories.title: Trussville Daybreak Rotary hosts aviation history presentation
stories.summary: The Trussville Daybreak Rotary Club held a Veterans Day program on 11 November featuring Dr. Brian Barsanti, Executive Director of the Southern Museum of Flight. The event included a presentation on Alabama’s aviation history for veterans in attendance. The club continues to honor local service members with guest speakers.

stories.title: The function of spoilers and lift dumpers on airliners
stories.summary: Spoilers are panels on an aircraft wing designed to destroy lift during landing. By disrupting airflow, these devices allow jets to descend steeply, stop on runways, and roll effectively. It is a device designed specifically to undo the primary purpose of the wing.

stories.title: ANA creates pilot training firm for upcoming retirements
stories.summary: ANA Holdings has launched ANA Next Aviation to manage pilot training as the airline prepares for retirements beginning around 2030. The firm will conduct basic training at Kagoshima Airport using actual aircraft. It is the first instance of a Japanese airline creating an in-house pilot training provider.

stories.title: Aerodynamics Academy hosts official AESA pilot examinations
stories.summary: Aerodynamics Academy in Spain has conducted its first official Airline Transport Pilot Licence and Private Pilot Licence theoretical examinations as an authorized center for the Aviation Safety Agency. The assessments were held at the academy's campus in Vélez-Málaga during the week commencing 16 November 2026.

research.title: Adaptive Control Barrier Functions for Nonlinear Singularly Perturbed Systems
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: Control barrier functions (CBFs) have emerged as a flexible and efficient approach for enforcing dynamic safety constraints. In this paper, we consider a class of uncertain nonlinear systems with singular perturbations and develop an adaptive CBF. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: Anomalous scaling of coalescence in a Hele-Shaw cell
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the merging of two drops between two narrowly spaced plates, a so-called Hele-Shaw cell. For this, we solve the Hele-Shaw equations in two dimensions, driven by surface tension, focusing on early times after initial. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: Efficient identification of finite impulse response systems under unknown or heavy-tailed noise remains a challenge in system identification. research.title: BridgeSRDA: Efficient Probabilistic Super-Resolution Data Assimilation with Forecast-Informed Stochastic Interpolants
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: High-resolution ensemble data assimilation is computationally demanding because it requires repeated forecasts and updates of many flow states. We introduce BridgeSRDA, a probabilistic super-resolution data assimilation framework that combines low-resolution numerical forecasts with sparse, noisy observations. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

Preprint, not peer reviewed.
